questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

“I know her well,​” said Manisha.

options.text: Manisha said that she knew her well.
Manisha said if she knows her well.
Manisha said that she knows her.
Manisha says that she knew her well

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Manisha said that she knew her well'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is **'Direct speech'** this we can see from the inverted commas.
 
• Before changing the direct speech following things should be kept in mind.
 
• The tense will change in the following way.
 
 
• **Present simple tense→ Past simple tense**
 
• **Past simple tense→ Past perfect tense.**
 
 
 
• The given sentence is in the** present simple tense **hence it will change into the **past simple tense.**
 
• The verb **'know**' becomes** 'knew' **and the **'that'** conjunction will be used.

**So according to this, the correct sentence is**→ *Manisha said that** she knew** her well.*

questions.question:
**A ****sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

She will finish the thesis in a fortnight.

options.text: The thesis would be finished in a fortnight by her.
The thesis will finished by her in a fortnight.
The thesis will be finished by her in a fortnight.
A fortnight is required to finish the thesis.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'The thesis will be finished by her in a fortnight'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• According to **the rule of **Active and Passive voice,** when we do transition** the** tense **of the sentence **doesn't change.**
 
• Also, the** subject **of the sentence** becomes the object **and the** object **of the sentence** becomes the subject.**
 
• In the given sentence, the** subject** is** 'she'** and the **object **is** 'thesis' **and the tense is the future tense.
 
• To change it into passive voice we use **'be + V₃'**

Therefore, the** correct answer is-** *The thesis will be finished by her in a fortnight. *

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blanks to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Sun is a ______ perfect sphere of hot plasma, with an ​internal convective motion that generates a magnetic field.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A description is being given about Sun.
 
• **“Nearly” **gives the closest essence as to describe the closeness to the term “perfect”.
 
• Also, in the given blank we need an** adverb **which is going to qualify an adjective 'perfect'.
 
 
• **​For example- **The audience was nearly all men.
 
 
 
• So, according to the above explanation the correct answer is 'Nearly

Therefore, the correct sentence is- *Sun is a nearly perfect sphere of hot plasma, with an ​internal convective motion that generates a magnetic field. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Near** is not agreeing with 'perfect' and is also generally used to describe proximity and distances.

 
 
• **For example**- I left the box near the door.
 
 
 
• **More** 'perfect' is grammatically incorrect as it is used for comparison while here sun is the only subject
 
 
• **For example**- You like more sugar in your tea than I do.
 
 
 
• **'About' **cannot fit as it cannot have “a” before it. We don’t say “Sun is a about…" 
 
 
• **For example**- Do you know anything about cricket?

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

She jumped ______ the bar table.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'upon'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given context, it is talking about jumping of a lady. 
 
• **Upon- **Used to show that one object has been placed on other object.
 
 
• **For example-** She was seated upon a throne. 
 
 
 
• Jumping up, into and in cannot be used as a table being a base, one cannot go inside it or jump upward. One can only jump across it, on it or upon it.
 
• So, according to above explanation 'Upon' is the best suitable choice.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is- *She jumped upon__ the bar table.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• Let's see the usage of other options.
 
• **Up-** Used to talk about a higher position or movement to a higher position 
 
 
• **For example-** He was up__ a ladder painting. 
 
 
 
• **In-** Used to indicate location or position within or inside something
 __
 
• **For example- **They have a house in __the country.
 
 
 
• **Into-** Used to a position in or inside something 
 __
 
• **For example-** She came into__ the room.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Due to the (1)/snow the (2)/marks was unrecognisable. (3)/No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'3' i.e. error lies in this part of the sentence.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In part 3 of the sentence,** the use of **'was' **is incorrect Instead, use '**were'**
 
• *According to the rule of subject-verb agreement, the verb should be plural if the subject of the sentence is plural.*
 
 
• ​**For example**- We were__ happy with the review of our first movie.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the subject is** 'marks'** hence the verb should be **'were'**
 
• **'Due to'** is a preposition and 'the snow' is the prepositional object hence there is no effect on the verb of 'the snow'.

**So the correct sentence is-** *Due to the snow** the marks were** unrecognisable.*
